statement.p: Calculate the Riemann sum for f(x,y)=4 x - 4 y and domain \mathcal{D} in Figure 2 with two choices of sample points, \bullet and \circ.
Which do you think is a better approximation to the integral of f over \mathcal{D} ? Why?

static.solution:
\Delta x=\Delta y=1 and area \Delta A=1\cdot 1=1.
(\bf a\it) Sample points \bullet. There are six sample points that lie in the domain \mathcal{D}.
We compute the values of f( x,y )=4 x - 4 y at these points:
\begin{array}{l}f( 1,1 )=0,\qquad\\ f( 2,1 )=4,\qquad\end{array}\begin{array}{l}f( 1,2 )=-4,\qquad\\ f( 2,2 )=0,\qquad\end{array}\begin{array}{l}f( 1,3 )=-8,\\ f( 2,3 )=-4\end{array}
The Riemann sum is
{S}_{3,4}=( 0 - 4 - 8+4+0 - 4)\cdot 1=-12 (\bf b\it)Sample points \circ.
We compute the values of f( x,y )=4 x - 4 y at the eight sample points that lie in \mathcal{D} :
\begin{array}{l}f( 1.5,0.5 )=4,\qquad\\ f( 1.5,3.5 )=-8,\end{array}\qquad\begin{array}{l}f( 0.5,1.5 )=-4,\qquad\\ f( 1.5,1.5 )=0,\qquad\\ f( 2.5,1.5 )=4,\qquad\end{array}\begin{array}{l}f( 0.5,2.5 )=-8,\\ f( 1.5,2.5 )=-4,\\ f( 2.5,2.5 )=0.\end{array} The corresponding Riemann sum is thus
{S}_{3,4}=(4 - 8 - 4 - 8+0 - 4+4+0 )\cdot 1=-16.
The approximation S_{3,4}(\circ) is the better approximation because it is calculated on more number of sample points. Also, its value is much closer to the actual value of the integral.
